correctness.rationale: An omitted leaf needs its core selected, excluding the doubly omitted arm. A selected leaf privately witnesses its omitted core automatically. A selected core witnessing its own omitted leaf cannot be adjacent in the base to an omitted core. These are precisely the adjacency rules of P3 with all loops, with the double selection at the middle. The mapping is invertible and the spin weight is z² at the middle and z at each endpoint. Dyer–Greenhill §5, not merely their generic constant-bound theorem, gives Widom–Rowlinson hardness with maximum degree three via nonsingularity of its adjacency matrix. The two-particle target is the connected reflexive path; the corrigendum's component issue does not remove this case. The map from the known hard problem preserves counts and increases the maximum degree by at most one. A subset and its witness property are verifiable in polynomial time, giving #P-completeness under polynomial-time Turing reductions. The contextual polynomial follows by making each induced endpoint component monochromatic; its cut coefficient read from |U|=n−1 has the stated equality only for connected bases of order at least two.
residual_risks: The finite replay only tests the count equality, not #P-hardness or all input sizes. Only the transfer map is parsimonious, not an asserted parsimonious reduction from every #P problem.

originality.rationale: For the repaired claim: exact enumeration and spin polynomial are existing, and the local admissibility needed for the bijection is prior on the corona side. The retained contribution is applying that structure to the two-species homomorphism problem to obtain exact counting hardness on coronas of subcubic bases. The strongest available earlier statements do not give the complexity classification of this graph problem.

value.rationale: The repaired result settles total counting complexity on a natural class with easy minimum size and minimum multiplicity. The spin interpretation provides a parsimonious transfer and a concrete low-degree restriction, not just a new summation of already known values. This identifies where exact all-set enumeration is hard even with a highly constrained graph construction.
residual_risks: No result about approximation, optimal degree threshold, tree-only bases, or different corona attachments.
